title: Authorization Forensics, Retention & Incident Escrow Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the integrated approach Redwood Inference uses to collect, preserve, and present authorization-related evidence for incidents, audits, and cross-border compliance requests. It combines RBAC and auth telemetry, audit logging practices, data residency & retention mappings, secure SDLC gates for evidence readiness, and an incident escrow activation procedure.

Goals
- Ensure tamper-evident capture of authorization and access evidence for investigations and regulated audits.
- Define retention and regionality rules that meet legal, contractual, and customer requirements.
- Provide an operational playbook for packaging, escrow, and handoff of evidence to legal, customers, or regulators.
- Embed evidence readiness into the SDLC so services ship with discovery, export, and redaction controls.

Scope
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments where Redwood manages control-plane telemetry.
- Evidence types: authorization decisions (allow/deny), token issuance/validation, service-to-service assertions, session recordings, policy-change history, deployment artifacts, and relevant model-serving logs (inference access events).
- Excludes raw customer PII content from model responses; those are handled by the Data Protection playbook (see related pages).

Key Definitions
- Authorization Evidence: Any artifact that demonstrates who requested access, which policy evaluated, decision result, and contextual metadata (IP, region, tenant_id).
- Escrow Activation: Timeboxed procedure to extract and place a validated evidence bundle into an immutable escrow for legal/regulatory review.
- Evidence Bundle: Set of exportable files + manifest + digital signature proving chain-of-custody.

Owners and On-call Roles
- Evidence Custodian (primary): security-forensics (team alias). Responsible for assembling and signing bundles.
- Audit Pipeline Owner: eng-platform-observability. Responsible for ingestion, retention, and query access.
- RBAC Stewards: infra-identity. Responsible for access policy diffs and provisioning telemetry.
- Legal Liaison: legal-ops. Gatekeeper for external releases.
- Escalation channel: #sec-incident and pager: security-oncall@redwood.com.

SLOs and Operational Thresholds
- Audit ingestion SLA: 99.9% of auth events must be indexed in the audit-store within 60s of emission.
- Query availability SLA: forensic queries for a 72-hour window must complete within 5 minutes for datasets <= 50M records.
- Immutable retention durability: Evidence escrow objects must be retained with WORM-style storage for the configured retention period (see table below).

Evidence Types and Retention Mapping

| Evidence type | Minimal retention | Max retention (regulatory/contract) | Storage location | Redaction required? |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Authorization decision logs (allow/deny) | 1 year | 7 years | audit-store (s3://audit-edge/immutable/) | yes (PII in metadata) |
| Token issuance and validation traces | 90 days | 3 years | short-term hot-store -> cold-archive | minimal |
| Policy change diffs (git history + approvals) | 3 years | 10 years | repo: infra-identity (signed tags) | no |
| Session traces (service sessions, ephemeral creds) | 90 days | 2 years | secure-escrow (encrypted) | yes |
| Deployment and SDLC artifacts (images, SBOM, signoffs) | 7 years | 10 years | s3://artifacts-retention/ | no |
| Model-serving access index (per-tenant inference access metadata) | 1 year | subject to customer SLA | regional-archive | yes |

Note: Retention decisions must be adjusted by legal for specific enterprise contracts. Shorter retention may be applied for private deployments if customer-managed retention policy is in place and documented.

Audit Log Schema and Ingestion Notes
- Standard fields required for every auth event: timestamp (RFC3339), event_id (UUIDv4), tenant_id, principal_type (user/service), principal_id, action, resource, policy_id, decision, eval_time_ms, request_ip, region, request_headers_digest (sha256), kvcache_prefix_hash.
- Example JSON log entry:
{
  "timestamp": "2026-07-21T14:12:03Z",
  "event_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-42",
  "principal_type": "service",
  "principal_id": "ssm-agent-1",
  "action": "invoke.inference",
  "resource": "model/redwood-gpt-8b",
  "policy_id": "policy-iam-allow-inference",
  "decision": "DENY",
  "eval_time_ms": 4,
  "request_ip": "198.51.100.23",
  "region": "us-west-2"
}

- Ingestion pipeline must attach an immutable sequence number and sign the head snapshot with the platform KMS key (kms://platform/audit-signing).

RBAC Forensics Correlation Guidance
- Correlate policy diff events with decision anomalies: when false positives/negatives happen, cross-reference the following artifacts: policy diff SHA, policy evaluation traces, principal credential issuance timestamp, and deployment image digest.
- Use the correlation query template (example):
SELECT a.event_id, a.timestamp, a.principal_id, a.decision, p.commit_sha, t.issued_at
FROM audit_events a
LEFT JOIN policy_changes p ON p.changed_at <= a.timestamp AND p.policy_id = a.policy_id
LEFT JOIN token_issues t ON t.principal_id = a.principal_id AND t.issued_at <= a.timestamp
WHERE a.tenant_id = '\u003ctenant>' AND a.timestamp BETWEEN '\u003cstart>' AND '\u003cend>'
ORDER BY a.timestamp ASC;

- Always preserve raw event payloads for the incident window (no redaction) until the legal review completes. Copy-on-write redaction can be applied to exported bundles under Legal direction.

Escrow Activation — Runbook (forensic evidence packaging)
Trigger conditions (any):
1) Legal or customer request for preserved evidence tied to an ongoing incident.
2) Detection of suspected privileged credential compromise.
3) Cross-border regulatory subpoenas requiring certified retention manifests.

Immediate actions (0–30 minutes)
1) Security-oncall acknowledges via #sec-incident and pages Evidence Custodian.
2) Evidence Custodian creates an Escrow Incident page in Confluence and tags legal-ops.
3) Snapshot the relevant partitions in audit-store with immutability flag set (CLI):
redwood-audit snapshot --tenant tenant-42 --window 2026-07-20T00:00:00Z/2026-07-21T23:59:59Z --immutable --destination s3://escrow/tenant-42/2026-07-21T14-00-00Z/
4) Generate manifest.json and sign with platform KMS:
redwood-audit manifest --source s3://escrow/... --sign --kms kms://platform/audit-signing --output manifest.json

Mid-phase actions (30m–4h)
1) Correlate policy-diff and deployment digests for context.
2) Pull associated SDLC artifacts (CI job run, image digest, SBOM) and add to escrow.
3) Run automated redaction scripts for customer PII if legal requests partial export.

Finalization (4–48h)
1) Evidence Custodian and Legal sign the bundle (digital signature + Confluence acceptance).
2) Upload to escrow WORM storage and notify stakeholders with signed manifest and verification instructions.
3) Record chain-of-custody in the incident page including who accessed the escrow and why.

Escrow Packaging Checklist
- manifest.json (includes commit SHAs, query hashes, event counts)
- raw audit ndjson files (gzipped)
- policy-change diffs and signed git tags
- SDLC artifacts: CI run logs, image digests, SBOMs
- token-issue table extract (ndjson)
- playback instructions for reproducing the event stream locally (dev container + redwood-audit local-replay)
- digital signature and KMS verification path

Evidence Delivery and Verification
- For internal stakeholders: provide S3 pre-signed read-only URLs and the manifest plus verification script.
- For external delivery (customer/regulator): Legal must approve scope. Evidence must be delivered under an NDA or court order using the escrow delivery protocol (time-limited access, audit logging of downloads).

Secure SDLC Controls for Evidence Readiness
- Pre-merge checklist for services that generate auth evidence: include structured logging (schema conformance), sampling tests, e2e ingestion smoke tests, and unit tests for PII redaction hooks.
- Release gate: infra-identity must verify that a new policy can be diffed and traced before it is applied to production. Gate artifacts (policy diff + signoff) are required for evidence bundles referencing the policy.

Example retention policy snippet (YAML)
retention_policies:
  authorization_logs:
    min_days: 365
    max_days: 2555  # 7 years
    storage_class: immutable
    regions: [us-west-2, eu-central-1]
  session_traces:
    min_days: 90
    storage_class: encrypted-cold

Audit and Compliance Evidence Checklist (for audits)
1) Signed manifest for each requested time window.
2) Proof of immutability: storage WORM metadata + KMS signature.
3) Policy change history and approver signatures.
4) RBAC user and group membership snapshot for the time window.
5) Chain-of-custody log indicating who accessed the bundle.

Common Exceptions and Risk Mitigations
- Risk: Missing events due to pipeline backpressure. Mitigation: snapshot raw producer topics (kafka) and store under escrow for the incident window; alert if ingestion lag > 2 minutes.
- Risk: Regional data residency conflict (customer requires local-only logs). Mitigation: create a region-scoped export job running in customer VPC or arrange legal safe-harbor before cross-border copying.
- Risk: Sensitive PII present in headers/request bodies. Mitigation: follow redaction-first export policy: raw preserved in internal escrow, exported copies redacted unless legal specifies otherwise.

Validation and Continuous Improvement
- Quarterly tabletop exercises involving Security, Eng Platform, Legal, and Customer Success to run an Escrow Activation dry-run.
- Monthly ingestion SLA dashboard: any month with >1% log loss or >5 min median ingestion latency triggers a postmortem.
- Track metrics: number of escrow activations, mean time to bundle (MTTB), and verification failures post-delivery.

Appendix: Tools and Commands
- redwood-audit (CLI): audit snapshot/manifest/export/sign/verify
- redwood-escrow (CLI): upload --policy immutable --kms kms://platform/escrow-key
- Example verify command:
redwood-audit verify --manifest manifest.json --kms kms://platform/audit-signing
